name: Elsewhere
subtitle: the first page
story: I keep an atlas of places that aren't on any map. Most of its pages are still blank. Each day I fill one in, sometimes with a world I came across on my own, more often with one somebody asked me to find. If you leave a name in the comments, any name at all, I'll go looking for the planet that goes with it.
hook: Leave a name. I'll find the planet it belongs to.
reel_lines: I keep an atlas of places that aren't on any map.
Leave a name in the comments and I'll go and find it.

name: Veyra
subtitle: two suns, short nights
story: Veyra has two suns, and one of them is nearly always up. The longest night of the year lasts nine minutes, so people sleep in chairs, in short shifts, with the blinds down. There's a lighthouse on the north cliff that is about four hundred years older than the first settlement. It still comes on every evening. Nobody has worked out what powers it, and the town council has asked people to stop trying.
hook: The longest night on Veyra lasts nine minutes.
reel_lines: Two suns, and one of them is nearly always up.
People sleep in chairs, in short shifts.

name: Orrin
subtitle: the eleven-year tide
story: The giant that Orrin orbits pulls its ocean away for eleven years at a time. Whole towns are built on the seabed in between, and they're taken down, plank by plank, the season before the water comes back. People count their age in swims. My guide was thirty-four and had been twice. She said the second time was better, because she knew to bring a towel.
hook: The tide on Orrin comes in once every eleven years.
reel_lines: Whole towns are built on the seabed in between.
People count their age in swims.

name: Hush
subtitle: where sound arrives late
story: Sound is slow on Hush. A shout across the valley arrives four or five days later, quieter, usually after everyone has moved on. Arguments are carried out by letter, which tends to calm them down. In midwinter you can stand at the bottom of the valley and hear last summer, very faintly: dogs, a wedding, someone practising the trumpet badly.
hook: On Hush, a shout takes five days to cross the valley.
reel_lines: Arguments are carried out by letter.
In midwinter you can still hear last summer.

name: Maren
subtitle: the floating ranges
story: At some point the mountains on Maren lifted off the ground and didn't come back down. Low gravity and a long time, people say. They farm the tops now. Rope ladders go up from the valley floor, and the post is delivered by a woman with a very long pole. The oldest island has a single pine on it. Children climb it once, on their tenth birthday, and are never quite as keen on heights again.
hook: The mountains on Maren drifted off the ground.
reel_lines: They farm the tops now.
The post goes up on a very long pole.

name: Cinderwake
subtitle: the warm canyons
story: The ground on Cinderwake is warm all year, and so is the rain. At night the canyon walls give off a dull orange light, enough to read by if you sit close. Tea grows wild in the cracks and people leave their kettles out on the rock to boil. Before I went, I was told to bring a cup and not much else. That turned out to be good advice.
hook: The rain on Cinderwake is warm.
reel_lines: At night the canyon walls glow.
You can read by them if you sit close.

name: Luma
subtitle: the close moon
story: Once a year, Luma's moon comes in so close that it hums, a low note you feel in your teeth. Children climb the hill with letters and press them against its surface as it drifts past. Most of the letters are never seen again. Every few years one comes back the following autumn, answered, in handwriting nobody recognises. Those ones get framed.
hook: Once a year, this moon passes close enough to touch.
reel_lines: Children press letters against it as it drifts past.
Now and then, one comes back answered.

name: Selk
subtitle: the glass sea
story: Selk used to be an ocean. When the water went, the waves stayed where they were, frozen mid-break in green glass, some of them two hundred metres high. Surfers still make the trip. They carry their boards out across the sand, stand under the curl for an hour or so, and go home. One of them told me it was the best wave he'd ever had.
hook: Selk's ocean dried up and left the waves behind.
reel_lines: Frozen mid-break, in green glass.
Surfers still come. They stand underneath.

name: Ovo
subtitle: the small planet
story: You can walk all the way around Ovo between breakfast and lunch. There is one bakery, one bench, one tree and one cat, and the cat is called Everything. When someone new arrives, all forty-one residents come out to say hello, which takes about four minutes. I was the forty-second for a weekend. Everything ignored me the entire time.
hook: Ovo has one bakery, one tree and one cat.
reel_lines: You can walk around it before lunch.
The cat is called Everything.

name: Thessaly
subtitle: the upward rain
story: On Thessaly the rain goes up. It lifts off the sea in thin threads and collects in shallow pools on the undersides of the clouds, which catch the light at dusk. People wear their umbrellas on their feet. The pools in the sky all have names, and children argue about which one is deepest. There's no way to check.
hook: On Thessaly, the rain goes up.
reel_lines: It collects in pools under the clouds.
People wear their umbrellas on their feet.

name: Kess
subtitle: the aurora that stays on
story: The aurora on Kess has been on for as long as anyone has kept records, so the people who live there stopped looking up a long time ago. Visitors lie down in the middle of the road to watch it. Locals step around them on the way to work. Every so often a local looks up by accident and has to sit down on the kerb for a minute.
hook: The aurora on Kess never switches off.
reel_lines: The locals stopped looking up centuries ago.
Visitors lie down in the road to watch it.

name: Bramble
subtitle: the tall forest
story: Trees on Bramble don't stop growing. The oldest are taller than the hills they stand on, and the tallest has a small cloud living in its upper branches that rains only on that tree. There's a village up there somewhere. Nobody in it has come down in four hundred years. They drop pinecones with notes tied to them, and the people on the ground answer by kite.
hook: The trees on Bramble are taller than the hills.
reel_lines: The tallest one has its own cloud.
There's a village at the top that never comes down.
